Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually and psychologically, including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Online Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms that targets women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, demeaning, or belittling of Women, messages or comments that threaten to commit physical or sexual violence against Women, disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims, extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless victims meet the perpetrator's demands, spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the women in the content, use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling victims, and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. I. GENERAL
Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights; therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and to guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and natural condition, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the Regional Government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, and environments located in the industrial sector.
Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement protection efforts for women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, guaranteeing the implementation of ease of services for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.
